extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary critics, and cultivated readers/aspiring poets
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for judging, composing, and understanding poetry and poetic genius — definitions of poem/poetry, distinctions between imagination and fancy, the plan for the Lyrical Ballads, and specific symptoms of original poetic power (illustrated by Shakespeare).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary vs Secondary Imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Imagination is either primary or secondary. The primary Imagination is the living power and prime agent of all human perception, 'a repetition in the finite mind of the eternal act of creation in the infinite I AM.' The secondary Imagination is an echo of the former, co-existing with the conscious will, identical in kind of agency but differing in degree and mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secondary Imagination 'dissolves, diffuses, dissipates, in order to recreate' and where that process is impossible 'struggles to idealize and to unify.' Emphasizes identity-in-kind with difference-in-degree; primary is essentially creative and formative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Fancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Fancy has no other counters to play with but 'fixities and definites.' It is 'no other than a mode of memory emancipated from the order of time and space,' blended with choice and receiving materials ready-made from the law of association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes fancy from Imagination by its passive, associative, and memory-based character; implies limits on what counts as genuinely creative poetic work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poem (final definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A poem is that species of composition which is opposed to works of science by proposing for its immediate object pleasure, not truth; and is discriminated from other species by proposing 'such delight from the whole, as is compatible with a distinct gratification from each component part.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes earlier allowances for metre/rhyme as superficial forms; stresses that if metre is superadded all parts must justify the recurrent attention metre provokes. A legitimate poem's parts must mutually support and explain each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimate Poem — unity of parts and continuous attention
rubrics_metrics.description: A legitimate poem is one whose parts mutually support and explain each other; all components harmonize with and support the purpose and known influences of metrical arrangement. The reader should be carried forward by the pleasurable activity of the journey itself, not merely by curiosity to reach the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejects (a) a series of striking lines or distiches each forming a separate whole and (b) an unsustained composition where the reader only collects a general result without being attracted by the component parts. Emphasizes proportional harmony and the reader's continuous engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry (broader notion) — relation to truth and prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry (in the strictest use) is closely tied to the poetic genius; poetry of the highest kind may exist without metre and sometimes has truth as its immediate object (e.g., portions of Isaiah). A poem of any length neither can be nor ought to be all poetry; remaining parts must be preserved in keeping by studied selection and arrangement to excite more continuous and equal attention than prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates limits to defining poetry by metre alone and requires artificial arrangement and selection to preserve poetic effect across a longer composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for Lyrical Ballads — two sorts of poems
rubrics_metrics.description: A series of poems might be composed of two sorts: (1) incidents and agents partly supernatural/romantic where excellence consists in interesting the affections by dramatic truth appropriate to such situations, and (2) subjects chosen from ordinary life where the object is to give novelty by awakening attention to the loveliness and wonders of everyday things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supernatural/romantic poems must transfer a human interest and semblance of truth sufficient to procure a 'willing suspension of disbelief' (poetic faith). Ordinary-life poems should use language of ordinary life to produce pleasurable interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willing suspension of disbelief / poetic faith
rubrics_metrics.description: For supernatural poems: transfer from our inward nature a human interest and semblance of truth sufficient to procure for these shadows of imagination that willing suspension of disbelief for the moment, which constitutes poetic faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetic success with supernatural subject matter depends on convincing emotional truth rather than literal plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of ordinary life (Wordsworth's stance and limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wordsworth proposed managing subjects that reject usual ornaments in the language of ordinary life to produce pleasurable interest; Coleridge notes the controversy and objects to extending that style indiscriminately to all poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns against a simplistic adoption of 'language of real life' for all poetry; style must suit subject and maintain poetic unity and dignity where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic Imagination as reconciling opposites
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagination is the power that reveals 'itself in the balance or reconcilement of opposite or discordant qualities' — of sameness with difference, the general with the concrete, idea with image, individual with representative, novelty with familiar, order with intense emotion, judgment with enthusiasm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This synthetic power subordinates art to nature, manner to matter, and admiration of the poet to sympathy with the poetry; it is the 'soul' of poetic genius that fuses faculties into unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet's ideal function — unity and subordination of faculties
rubrics_metrics.description: The ideal poet 'brings the whole soul of man into activity, with the subordination of its faculties to each other according to their relative worth and dignity.' He diffuses a tone and spirit of unity by Imagination that fuses each faculty into a graceful and intelligent whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good Sense is the body of poetic genius; Fancy its drapery; Motion its life; Imagination its soul — these must coordinate for poetic excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific symptom 1: Musical sweetness of versification
rubrics_metrics.description: Perfect sweetness of versification, adaptation to the subject, and power in varying the march of words without passing into a loftier rhythm than required. 'The delight in richness and sweetness of sound'—a sense of musical delight is a gift of Imagination and a favourable promise in young writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Musical delight is not merely craft or imitation; it is an original gift ('poeta nascitur non fit'). Versification must suit thought and sustain melody appropriate to subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific symptom 2: Choice of subjects remote from the author's private interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Genius is promised when subjects are chosen remote from the author's private experiences; when the subject is too autobiographical it often signals only acquired skill or trade, not original genius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive reliance on personal sensations as material can be a fallacious pledge of genius; genuine poetic power often manifests in convincingly rendering lives and passions beyond the poet's own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific symptom 3: Imagery animated by a predominant passion
rubrics_metrics.description: Images, however beautiful, become proofs of original genius only as they are modified by a predominant passion, associated thoughts or images, reduce multitude to unity, or have human and intellectual life transferred from the poet's spirit into them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by transforming descriptive lines into imagery that carries passion and unity; imagery must serve a larger intellectual or emotional synthesis rather than mere decoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific symptom 4: Depth and energy of thought (philosophic profundity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depth and energy of thought are indispensable; 'No man was ever yet a great poet, without being at the same time a profound philosopher.' Poetry is the blossom of human knowledge and thought; creative power and intellectual energy must wrestle and be reconciled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without philosophic depth, imagination's flashes are transitory; sustained greatness combines imaginative power with wide knowledge, reflection, and intellectual energy.
